day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight AC lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Use the morning to rest or prepare for landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Old Montreal Stay and drop off luggage. Take a self-guided walk through Vieux-Montréal to get oriented — stroll along Rue Saint-Paul, admire the Notre-Dame Basilica exterior (free to view outside), and soak in the cobblestone atmosphere. Head to the Old Port waterfront for fresh air and city views along the St. Lawrence River.
day_by_day.evening: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk — Join an evening guided walk through the historic cobblestone streets, stopping for poutine, smoked meat sandwiches, and other Quebec street food classics. A perfect low-cost introduction to the city's culinary identity right from your hotel's neighbourhood.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at Montréal-Trudeau Airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick and affordable smoked meat sandwich or bagel from a deli near the Old Port (~$10–14 CAD).
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Street Food & History Walk tastings; supplement with a classic poutine from La Banquise's Old Montreal outlet or a nearby casse-croûte (~$12–16 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Since arrival is at 13:00, factor in ~45–60 minutes for baggage claim and transit to Old Montreal (STM bus 747 to downtown, then transfer, or taxi ~$45 CAD flat rate). Keep Day 1 light and walkable — everything is within easy reach of your hotel on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour — Take the Metro (Orange Line) north to Jean-Talon station for a guided or self-guided tour of one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample local Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh produce, artisan breads, and charcuterie. Arrive early (9:00–10:00) for the best atmosphere and freshest stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mile End and Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhoods on foot or by BIXI bike (Montreal's affordable bike-share, ~$7 CAD/day). Browse colourful murals, independent boutiques, and the famous Schwartz's Deli. Walk through Parc La Fontaine, a beautiful free green space perfect for a picnic with market finds.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Street Shows — Head to the Quartier des Spectacles or Saint-Denis Street for FREE outdoor comedy performances as part of North America's largest comedy festival (running mid-July). Enjoy world-class stand-up and street acts under the warm summer sky at no cost.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh Montreal-style bagel with cream cheese from a bakery near Old Montreal or the hotel (~$4–6 CAD).
meals.lunch: Eat at Jean-Talon Market — assemble a budget picnic from market vendors: local cheese, baguette, fruit, and maple treats (~$12–15 CAD total).
meals.dinner: Affordable dinner in the Plateau: try a BYOB (apportez votre vin) restaurant like Pintxo or a local Vietnamese pho spot on Saint-Denis (~$15–20 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: A 10-ride Metro pass (~$33 CAD) is excellent value for the trip. BIXI bikes are a fun and cheap way to cover the Plateau and Mile End. Just for Laughs free shows require no tickets — just show up early for a good spot.

day_by_day.morning: Mont Royal Park — Take a morning hike or walk up to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout on Mount Royal for panoramic views of the city skyline. The park is completely free and beloved by locals. Rent a BIXI bike at the base for a scenic ride through the park's trails. Arrive by 9:00 for cooler temperatures and fewer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience — While this festival has a winter edition, its summer programming features pop-up chef experiences, outdoor food tastings, and cultural performances in the Quartier des Spectacles. Explore the free outdoor programming and sample affordable festival bites from local Quebec chefs and food vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Just for Laughs Festival for ticketed indoor shows (budget seats available from ~$20–35 CAD) or continue enjoying the free outdoor gala performances and street acts near Saint-Denis and Sainte-Catherine streets. The festive Friday-night energy in the Quartier des Spectacles is electric.

meals.breakfast: Cook simple breakfast at the hotel if kitchen facilities are available, or grab a croissant and café au lait from a local boulangerie (~$5–7 CAD).
meals.lunch: Grab a crêpe or a Quebecois tourtière slice from a food truck or market stall near the festival grounds (~$10–13 CAD).
meals.dinner: Try a classic Québécois sugar shack-style meal at a budget cabane à sucre pop-up, or dine at a BYOB restaurant in the Latin Quarter near Saint-Denis (~$16–22 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Mont Royal is a 20-minute bus ride from Old Montreal (Bus 11 from Guy-Concordia Metro). Wear comfortable walking shoes for the hill. Check the Just for Laughs official schedule in advance to reserve any ticketed shows you want — free shows need no reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Marché Atwater — Visit this charming covered market near the Lachine Canal for a final taste of Montreal's local food scene. Browse artisan cheeses, fresh pastries, Quebec microbrews, and seasonal produce. Pick up affordable souvenirs like maple syrup, local jams, or a tin of smoked salmon to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lachine Canal Walk or Bike Ride — Rent a BIXI bike and follow the scenic Lachine Canal path westward. The flat, paved trail is free and runs alongside historic locks and industrial heritage sites. Stop at a waterside park for a picnic lunch with your Atwater Market finds. Return to Old Montreal in the early afternoon to explore any last corners of Vieux-Montréal you may have missed.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Old Montreal — Enjoy a farewell stroll along the illuminated cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal. Catch any remaining Just for Laughs street performances near Place des Arts or the Quartier des Spectacles. End the trip with a classic Quebec dessert — a warm sugar pie (tarte au sucre) or maple soft-serve — from a local café.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastry and coffee from Marché Atwater's in-market bakery (~$6–8 CAD).
meals.lunch: Picnic along the Lachine Canal with market finds: cheese, baguette, charcuterie, and local fruit (~$12–15 CAD).
meals.dinner: Budget-friendly farewell dinner at a well-loved Old Montreal spot — try Olive et Gourmando for gourmet sandwiches or L'Gros Luxe for affordable comfort food with a Quebec twist (~$15–20 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: If departing on Day 5 or later, pack bags the night before and store luggage at the hotel. The STM 747 bus offers affordable airport transfers (~$11 CAD). Check festival schedules one last time — Saturday evenings often feature the biggest free outdoor performances of the Just for Laughs weekend lineup.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal-Trudeau Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Old Montreal Stay hotel (~30 min by taxi or express bus 747). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighbourhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk: After settling in, step right outside your hotel door and explore the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal. Stop at iconic spots for classic poutine, smoked meat sandwiches, and Quebec-style snacks while soaking up the 17th-century architecture of Place Jacques-Cartier and the Old Port waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Old Port promenade at sunset, then catch any free outdoor performances happening near Place des Arts or the waterfront as part of the Just for Laughs Festival Street Shows — July is peak festival season and free street acts run nightly throughout downtown.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a casual café near the hotel upon arrival (~$15–20 CAD)
meals.dinner: Crew Café or Olive & Gourmando in Old Montreal — beloved local bistro serving Quebec-inspired dishes; expect ~$35–50 CAD per person including a glass of local cider

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light given the 13:00 arrival. The Old Montreal Street Food Walk is walkable directly from the hotel — no transit needed. Pack a light rain layer just in case of afternoon showers. July is Just for Laughs Festival month, so check the free street show schedule at hahaha.com for evening pop-up times near the Old Port.

day_by_day.morning: Mile End Bagel & Brunch Crawl: Take the metro (Orange Line, ~20 min from Place-d'Armes to Laurier station) to the beloved Mile End neighbourhood. Visit the legendary wood-fired Fairmount Bagel and St-Viateur Bagel bakeries, sampling fresh-out-of-the-oven sesame and poppy seed bagels with cream cheese and smoked salmon. Browse the hip, artsy streets lined with murals and independent boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Head to Jean-Talon Market (a short bus or metro ride from Mile End, ~10 min). Explore one of North America's largest open-air markets, sampling local Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh seasonal produce, charcuterie, and artisan jams. Pick up snacks and local specialties to bring back to the hotel. Take your time — the market is lively and vibrant on summer afternoons.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Street Shows: Return toward downtown for the evening and catch free outdoor comedy performances near the festival hub around Rue Saint-Denis and Place des Arts. If budget allows, consider a ticketed indoor show (~$40–70 CAD) featuring well-known comedians for a quintessential Montreal summer experience.

meals.breakfast: Fairmount Bagel in Mile End — fresh bagel with cream cheese and lox (~$8–12 CAD); iconic and unmissable
meals.lunch: Jean-Talon Market lunch: assemble a picnic-style spread from market vendors — local cheese, cured meats, fresh bread, and seasonal fruit (~$20–25 CAD)
meals.dinner: Damas or Lemeac on Laurier Avenue West — upscale-casual Montreal dining with seasonal Quebec ingredients; ~$45–60 CAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Mile End and Jean-Talon involve a lot of pleasant strolling. Bring a reusable bag for market purchases. Jean-Talon Market is busiest mid-morning to early afternoon on weekdays — arriving around 11:00 is ideal. Check Just for Laughs schedule in advance for the best free street acts.

day_by_day.morning: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience (Summer Edition): While traditionally a winter festival, the summer programming features world-class chef pop-ups, outdoor culinary showcases, and cultural performances. Start the morning by attending any scheduled chef demonstrations or food market activations. If summer programming is limited, substitute with a visit to Marché Atwater — a beautiful indoor-outdoor market near the Lachine Canal — for artisan breads, local cheeses, and Quebec wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood: Wander up to Parc La Fontaine for a relaxed afternoon picnic using morning market finds. Rent a bike from BIXI (Montreal's bike-share, ~$8 CAD/day) and cycle the scenic Lachine Canal path, a beloved local activity connecting the city's green spaces. Stop at local independent cafés and boutiques along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Old Montreal for dinner, then enjoy a guided evening walking tour of the illuminated historic district — many operators offer 90-minute tours departing from Place d'Armes (~$25–30 CAD). Cap the night with a cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the St. Lawrence River.

meals.breakfast: Café Olimpico in Mile End or a local bakery near the hotel — croissant, café au lait (~$10–14 CAD)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Parc La Fontaine with market provisions, or grab a crêpe and fresh juice from a Plateau street vendor (~$15–20 CAD)
meals.dinner: Le Filet or Maison Boulud in Old Montreal — sophisticated yet mid-range-friendly Quebec seafood and contemporary French cuisine; ~$50–65 CAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings in July are especially lively in Old Montreal and the Plateau. BIXI bikes are available at docking stations throughout the city — download the app beforehand. If the Montreal en Lumière summer edition is not running on this specific date, the morning slot works perfectly for a relaxed Marché Atwater visit instead.

day_by_day.morning: Mount Royal Morning Hike: Start the final day with an invigorating walk up Mont Royal Park — a 30-minute walk or short bus ride from Old Montreal. Follow the wooded Olmsted Trail to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for panoramic views of the city skyline and the St. Lawrence River. Locals jog, picnic, and drum at the famous tam-tams gathering (held every Sunday, but Saturday mornings are peaceful and beautiful).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last exploration of Old Montreal & Souvenir Shopping: Return to Vieux-Montréal for a final leisurely afternoon. Visit the stunning Notre-Dame Basilica (entry ~$15 CAD), browse artisan galleries and boutiques on Rue Saint-Paul, and pick up Quebec-made souvenirs — local maple syrup, ice cider, and artisan chocolates. Enjoy one last stroll along the Old Port.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Old Montreal, followed by a relaxed evening along the waterfront. If any Just for Laughs Festival closing shows or Montreal en Lumière events are scheduled, this is the perfect night to attend as a festive send-off to the trip.

meals.breakfast: Crew Café or Café Parvis near Old Montreal — avocado toast, eggs, fresh-pressed juice (~$15–20 CAD)
meals.lunch: L'Original or Satay Brothers food truck near Old Port — casual, flavourful, and locally loved; ~$18–25 CAD
meals.dinner: Garde Manger or Liverpool House in Old Montreal — celebratory farewell dinner with locally sourced Quebec ingredients and a lively atmosphere; ~$55–75 CAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Check departure logistics on Day 4 evening or Day 5 morning — Old Montreal is well-connected to the airport via taxi (~35 min) or 747 express bus (~45 min). Pack Quebec market finds carefully — maple syrup and cheese travel well. Saturday evenings in July are the most festive in the city, so expect lively streets and spontaneous performances throughout Old Montreal and downtown.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk: After settling in, embark on a guided cobblestone stroll through Vieux-Montréal. Visit iconic spots for Montreal's legendary poutine, smoked meat sandwiches, and artisan pastries. Explore Place Jacques-Cartier, the Bonsecours Market, and the historic waterfront promenade along the St. Lawrence River.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Street Shows: Head to the St-Denis/Quartier Latin area (short taxi or rideshare ride) to catch the free outdoor comedy performances of the Just for Laughs Festival. Enjoy world-class street performers, pop-up comedy acts, and the electric summer festival atmosphere under the warm July evening sky.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport dining prior to arrival.
meals.lunch: Light welcome bite at the hotel or a quick stop at a nearby Old Montreal café such as Olive + Gourmando for artisan sandwiches and freshly baked goods.
meals.dinner: Toqué! — Montreal's iconic fine-dining institution steps from Old Montreal. Chef Normand Laprise's celebrated tasting menu showcases the finest Quebec terroir ingredients. Reserve the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing for a truly premium first-night experience.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer in advance. The Just for Laughs Festival runs mid-July and many street shows are free — check the official schedule for ticketed headline acts if desired. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the cobblestone streets. Weather should be warm (~25°C), ideal for evening outdoor festival strolling.

day_by_day.morning: Mile End Bagel & Brunch Crawl: Start the day in Montreal's beloved bohemian Mile End neighbourhood. Visit the legendary Fairmount Bagel and St-Viateur Bagel bakeries — both wood-fired institutions open since dawn — to taste freshly baked sesame and poppy seed bagels. Stroll along St-Viateur Street, browsing independent boutiques and street art before a leisurely brunch stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Head to Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest and most celebrated open-air markets. Join a premium guided tasting tour sampling local Quebec cheeses, artisan charcuterie, maple products, fresh berries, and heritage vegetables directly from farmers and specialty vendors. Pick up premium local provisions and engage with passionate Quebec producers.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal en Lumière Festival Experience: Experience a curated summer edition pop-up of the Montreal en Lumière festival, featuring world-class chef collaborations, gourmet tasting events, and illuminated outdoor installations. Enjoy a multi-course collaborative dinner experience at one of the festival's premier participating restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Fairmount Bagel in Mile End — fresh wood-fired bagels with smoked salmon, cream cheese, and capers. Simple, iconic, and quintessentially Montreal.
meals.lunch: Provisions sourced at Jean-Talon Market arranged as a premium picnic, or dine at Damas — an acclaimed upscale Syrian-Mediterranean restaurant steps from the market, celebrated for its refined mezze and seasonal tasting menus.
meals.dinner: Le Mousso — an avant-garde tasting menu restaurant by chef Antonin Mousseau-Rivard, known for bold, inventive Quebec-inspired cuisine. Book the full tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is liveliest in the morning and early afternoon — the guided tour ideally begins around 1:00–2:00 PM. Arrange a private driver or use the Metro (Orange Line, Jean-Talon station) for comfortable transit between Mile End and the market. Confirm Montreal en Lumière summer programming and restaurant reservations well in advance as seats sell out quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Just for Laughs Festival — Premium Ticketed Gala Experience: Begin the morning leisurely with a late hotel breakfast, then review the day's Just for Laughs Festival lineup. Head to the festival hub around mid-morning to explore the outdoor free stages, merchandise, and interactive comedy installations along Rue St-Denis. Catch impromptu street performances and international comedians warming up the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal & Vieux-Port Exploration: Return to your home base in Old Montreal for a curated afternoon. Visit the Pointe-à-Callière Museum of Archaeology and History for a premium private guided tour of Montreal's founding site and underground archaeological ruins. Afterward, take a scenic electric boat cruise on the St. Lawrence River for panoramic views of the city skyline and the historic port.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival — Headline Gala Show: Attend a premium ticketed headline gala at the Théâtre St-Denis or Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier. These world-class comedy galas feature internationally renowned headliners in an elegant theatre setting — the pinnacle of the festival experience. Dress smart-casual for the occasion.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel premium breakfast at your Old Montreal Stay property, or visit Crew Collective & Café in the stunning neoclassical Royal Bank building for a lavish morning spread.
meals.lunch: Garde Manger — celebrity chef Chuck Hughes' beloved Old Montreal restaurant known for its indulgent lobster poutine, oysters, and elevated comfort food. Perfect for a leisurely weekend-eve lunch.
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner at Maison Boulud in the Ritz-Carlton Montreal — Chef Daniel Boulud's Montreal outpost offering refined French-Canadian cuisine in an opulent setting. Order the seasonal prix-fixe with sommelier wine pairings before heading to the gala.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Just for Laughs gala tickets months in advance — premium and VIP packages sell out rapidly. The festival atmosphere peaks on Friday evening with street parties and outdoor stages buzzing until late. Weather at 25°C makes evening outdoor festival exploration very pleasant. Keep an umbrella handy given the month's average rainfall.

day_by_day.morning: Montreal en Lumière — Chef's Market Breakfast & Culinary Workshop: Begin your final morning with an exclusive culinary experience tied to the Montreal en Lumière festival — a private chef-led market breakfast or hands-on Quebec cooking workshop focusing on local seasonal ingredients, artisan cheeses, and maple-forward cuisine. This intimate experience is the perfect luxury farewell to Montreal's food culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure & Luxury Spa Afternoon: Return to Old Montreal for a relaxed, indulgent afternoon. Book a premium spa treatment at the Scandinave Spa Vieux-Montréal — an urban Nordic spa featuring thermal baths, steam rooms, and massage treatments in a beautifully designed Old Montreal setting. Alternatively, browse the high-end boutiques and galleries of Rue Notre-Dame Ouest for artisan Quebec souvenirs and luxury goods.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Old Montreal Sunset Stroll: Conclude your premium Montreal journey with a spectacular farewell dinner, followed by a golden-hour stroll along the Vieux-Port waterfront. Watch the sunset over the St. Lawrence River and soak in the magical atmosphere of one of North America's most enchanting cities.

meals.breakfast: Part of the culinary workshop experience, or enjoy a luxurious in-hotel breakfast with Quebec cheeses, fresh fruit, viennoiseries, and locally roasted coffee.
meals.lunch: Nora Gray — an acclaimed Italian-inspired restaurant in the Griffintown neighbourhood, celebrated for its impeccable seasonal pasta and natural wine list. A refined, relaxed Saturday lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Vin Papillon or Joe Beef (sister restaurants by chefs David McMillan and Frédéric Morin) in Little Burgundy — among the most celebrated dining destinations in Canada. Joe Beef's legendary indulgent menu of foie gras, fresh seafood, and Quebec classics is the ultimate luxury farewell dinner. Reserve the chef's table if available.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange late checkout or luggage storage if your departure flight is in the evening. Scandinave Spa Vieux-Montréal is walking distance from Old Montreal Stay — book treatments in advance. Joe Beef is notoriously difficult to book; reserve as early as possible or ask your hotel concierge to assist. This final day balances culinary immersion, relaxation, and a memorable send-off perfectly aligned with the premium trip style.
